title: Biodiversity and its measurement; Adaptations; Ecosystems, populations and niches
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EC01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; EC01a#t4 term and clue written for the game; EC01a#t3 term and clue written for the game; EV07b#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EC01a#N.3a, EV07b#N.4b, EV09#N.3, EC01a#N.5, EV09#N.18, EC01a#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Population
items.clue: All the organisms of one species in one area at one time

items.label: Abiotic factors
items.clue: Non-living influences such as temperature, light, pH and salinity

items.label: Ecosystem
items.clue: All the living things in an area together with their non-living environment

items.label: Alleles
items.clue: What members of one species differ in, although they all have the same genes

questions.stem: Two groups of great crested newts breed in ponds 5 km apart, and no newt ever moves between the ponds. How should the two groups be described?

options.text: Two populations of one species, because the groups are reproductively isolated from each other.
Two species, because groups that do not interbreed cannot belong to the same species.
One population, because all the newts belong to the same species, wherever they breed.
Two communities, because each pond contains newts together with the other organisms living in it.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. 80 voles from an island population were tested at one locus. 20 were heterozygous, 45 homozygous dominant and 15 homozygous recessive. What is the heterozygosity index, H?

options.text: A rattlesnake's venom is an anatomical adaptation, because it is delivered through the fangs.
Zebras living in herds is not an adaptation, because behaviour is not inherited.
A kangaroo rat producing very concentrated urine is a physiological adaptation.
A dog moved to a cold country growing a thicker coat during its life is an anatomical adaptation.

questions.explanation: It is a body process, carried out by the kidneys, that saves water in the desert.

questions.stem: A student finds a woodland plant only on the shaded side of a hedge. Which pair names one abiotic factor and one biotic factor that could explain this?

options.text: Light intensity; soil pH
A grazing rabbit; a competing grass
Light intensity; a competing grass
Soil water; air temperature

questions.explanation: Light is non-living (abiotic); a competitor is living (biotic). Either could restrict the plant to the shaded side.

questions.stem: Arctic foxes have much smaller ears than fennec foxes. Which statement best explains how small ears became typical of Arctic foxes?

options.text: Each Arctic fox's ears shrank during its life in the cold, and its cubs inherited the smaller ears.
Foxes with alleles for smaller ears lost less heat, so survived and bred more; the alleles spread.
The cold caused new mutations for small ears to arise in the foxes that needed them.
Small ears are better in every environment, so in time all foxes will evolve them.

questions.stem: A fallen, rotting log in a wood holds beetle larvae, woodlice, fungi and bacteria. Inside it are damp, decaying wood and still air. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The log cannot be an ecosystem, because an ecosystem must cover a large area such as a forest.
The log's organisms, with its damp wood and still air, form a small ecosystem.
All the organisms living in the log together form one population.
The fungi and bacteria are not part of the community, because they are neither animals nor plants.

questions.explanation: A community plus its abiotic environment is an ecosystem, whether it is a log, a rock pool or a rainforest.
